answer: Each identity claims one river reach and locks a 70-credit bond in a vault. It files a key-signed survey of the reach's channel prism: width, depth, length. An auditor remeasures the reach and recomputes the prism volume; a mismatch, reused survey, or second claim on the same reach burns the bond. The first claim pays 34; the kth pays 34+7(k-1), so the 1000th pays 7027 and 1000 fakes pay 3,530,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-survey ring fails because the auditor's own remeasurement decides, and one key holds one reach. An honest agent locks 70 once and pays 34 once.
